stimuli.text: A solid insulating sphere of radius R = 0.08 m has a total charge Q = +1 nC distributed uniformly throughout its volume.
An initially uncharged 15 µF capacitor, a 20 kΩ resistor, an ideal 6 V battery and an open switch are connected in series. The switch is closed at t = 0.
Students measure the resistance of different lengths of a wire with a diameter of 0.5 mm, using a battery, an ammeter and a voltmeter.

A conducting rod of mass 0.2 kg and length 0.7 m slides without friction on horizontal rails connected by a 2 Ω resistor. A uniform 0.8 T magnetic field points vertically through the rails. The rod is given an initial speed of 4 m/s and then released.

questions.stem: A 80-turn coil of area 0.12 m² is perpendicular to a magnetic field that changes by 0.7 T in 0.9 s. What is the magnitude of the average induced emf?

options.why: Multiply by the number of turns.

questions.stem: A flat circular coil of 6 turns and radius 0.12 m carries 15 A. What is the field at its center?

options.why: That is a straight wire's field.

questions.stem: A 39 µF capacitor is charged to 135 V. How much energy does it store?
The current in a wire is $$I(t) = 6t^2$$ A. How much charge passes a point from $$t = 0$$ to $$t = 5$$ s?
Two parallel plates 0.02 m apart have a potential difference of 150 V. What is the field between them?

options.why: Correct. In a uniform field, E = ΔV/d.

questions.stem: Two identical small conducting spheres carry 7 µC and 8 µC. They are touched together and separated. What is the charge on each?

options.why: The total is shared between two spheres.
Correct. Identical conductors share the total charge equally.

questions.explanation: Total 15 µC, split equally: 7.5 µC each.

questions.stem: A solenoid 0.2 m long has 500 turns and carries 7 A. What is the magnetic field inside it?

options.why: That resembles a wire's field; use B = μ₀nI.
Correct. B = μ₀nI with n = N/L.

questions.stem: A long straight wire carries a uniform charge of 6 µC/m. What is the field 0.13 m from it?

options.why: A line charge's field falls off as 1/r.
Correct. E = λ/(2πε₀r), from Gauss's law with a cylinder.

questions.stem: A battery with emf 21 V and internal resistance 0.6 Ω is connected to a 12 Ω resistor. What is the current?

options.why: Correct. I = ε/(R + r); V = ε − Ir.

questions.stem: A proton moves at $$8 \times 10^{5}$$ m/s perpendicular to a uniform 0.05 T magnetic field. What is the radius of its path?

options.why: Correct. qvB = mv²/r, so r = mv/(qB).

questions.stem: Point P is 0.2 m from a +5 µC charge and 0.4 m from a −9 µC charge. What is the electric potential at P?

options.why: Correct. Potential is a scalar: add kq/r with signs.
The negative charge contributes negative potential.

questions.stem: A long straight wire carries 25 A. What is the magnetic field 0.06 m from it?

options.why: A long wire's field falls off as 1/r.
That is the field at the center of a loop.

questions.stem: A 0.3 m conducting rod slides at 17 m/s along rails connected by a 14 Ω resistor, perpendicular to a uniform 0.2 T field. What is the induced current?

options.why: Correct. ε = BLv, I = ε/R, F = ILB = B²L²v/R.
That is the emf, in volts.

questions.stem: Point P is 0.2 m from a +5 µC charge and 0.2 m from a −4 µC charge. What is the electric potential at P?

options.why: Correct. Potential is a scalar: add kq/r with signs.
The negative charge contributes negative potential.

questions.stem: A uniform field of 900 N/C passes through a flat 0.9 m² surface whose normal makes 60° with the field. What is the flux through the surface?

options.why: θ is measured from the normal, so use cos θ.

questions.stem: A 20 µF capacitor starts uncharged and is charged through a 460 kΩ resistor by a 15 V battery. What is the capacitor's voltage after 18.4 s?

options.why: Convert kΩ and µF to Ω and F.
Correct. τ = RC = 9.2 s; V = ε(1 − e^(−t/τ)).
That is the charging resistor's voltage.
The change is exponential, not linear.

questions.stem: A 0.3 m wire carrying 6 A makes a 60° angle with a uniform 0.3 T magnetic field. What is the magnitude of the magnetic force on it?

options.why: Use sin θ, from the cross product.

questions.stem: The current in a 0.05 H inductor changes by 8 A in 0.15 s. What is the magnitude of the average induced emf?

options.why: That is power from energy; use ε = L dI/dt.

questions.stem: A 12 µF capacitor is in parallel with a series combination of 4 µF and 3 µF. What is the equivalent capacitance?

options.why: Not all the capacitors are in series.
Not all the capacitors are in parallel.
Correct. Capacitors add in parallel; reciprocals add in series.
The series and parallel rules are swapped (they are the reverse of resistors).

questions.stem: Two point charges of 9 µC and −5 µC are 0.34 m apart. What is the magnitude of the force between them?
An electron starts from rest and is accelerated through a potential difference of 650 V. What is its final speed? ($$m_e = 9.11 \times 10^{-31}$$ kg)
A parallel-plate capacitor has plates of area 0.11 m² separated by 7 mm, filled with a dielectric of κ = 3.5. What is its capacitance?
How much work must an external agent do to move a +1 µC charge slowly from a point at 125 V to a point at 43 V?
A 4 Ω resistor is connected across 30 V. What power does it dissipate?
A solid insulating sphere of radius 0.05 m has 5 µC distributed uniformly through its volume. What is the field magnitude 0.01 m from its center?

options.why: Only the charge inside radius r counts.
Correct. Inside, the enclosed charge is Q(r/R)³, so E = kQr/R³.
That is the field at the surface.

questions.stem: A wire 41 m long has a diameter of 2.9 mm and resistivity $$2.8 \times 10^{-8}$$ Ω·m. What is its resistance?

options.why: Correct. R = ρL/A with A = π(d/2)².

questions.stem: A parallel-plate capacitor has plates of area 0.12 m² separated by 5 mm, filled with a dielectric of κ = 3.5. What is its capacitance?
A ring of radius 0.3 m carries 7 µC spread uniformly. What is the field magnitude on its axis 0.33 m from the center?

options.why: Only the axial components add; the others cancel.
The charge is not at the center.

questions.stem: A conducting sphere of radius 1 cm carrying 32 nC is connected by a long thin wire to an uncharged conducting sphere of radius 7 cm far away. What charge ends up on the smaller sphere?

options.why: That is the larger sphere's charge.
Correct. Connected spheres reach equal potential, so Q ∝ R.
Equal potential gives Q ∝ R, not R².

questions.explanation: kQ₁/R₁ = kQ₂/R₂ with Q₁ + Q₂ = 32: Q₁ = 4 nC.

questions.stem: Charges of -3 µC, 1 µC, 5 µC sit at the corners of an equilateral triangle with sides 0.2 m. What is the system's electric potential energy?

options.why: Correct. Add kqᵢqⱼ/r for all three pairs.
Keep the signs of the charges.

questions.stem: Charges of +5 µC and +8 µC are 1 m apart. What is the magnitude of the electric field at the midpoint between them?

options.why: The distance is d/2, so r² = d²/4.
Each charge is d/2 from the midpoint.
Correct. Like charges' fields point in opposite directions at the midpoint: subtract.
Check the directions of the two fields at the midpoint.

questions.explanation: Each field is k q/(d/2)²: 1.8 \times 10^{5} and 2.88 \times 10^{5} N/C, opposite, giving 1.08 \times 10^{5} N/C.

questions.stem: A parallel-plate capacitor is charged and then disconnected from the battery. A dielectric with κ = 4 is inserted to fill the gap. What happens to the capacitor's charge?

options.why: Each quantity changes by at most a factor of κ.
Decide first whether Q or V is held fixed.
Each quantity changes by at most a factor of κ.
Correct. Disconnected, Q is fixed and C rises by κ.

questions.explanation: C becomes κC. Q fixed: V = Q/C and U = Q²/(2C) fall by κ.

questions.stem: A single loop contains a 22 V battery and a 2 V battery connected so their emfs oppose each other, plus resistors of 6 Ω and 4 Ω. What is the current?

options.why: Both resistors are in the loop.
Correct. Loop rule: ε₁ − ε₂ − I(R₁ + R₂) = 0.

questions.stem: A 4 Ω resistor is in series with a parallel pair of 7 Ω and 12 Ω, connected to an ideal 13 V battery. What is the current in the 7 Ω resistor?

options.why: Only part of the battery's voltage is across the pair.
Correct. Reduce the parallel pair, add the series resistor, then work back.

questions.stem: A charge of +16q is at $$x = 0$$ and a charge of +q is at $$x = 3$$ m. At what point between them is the electric field zero?

options.why: Compare r², so take square roots.
The zero point is closer to the smaller charge.

questions.stem: The electric potential along the x-axis is $$V(x) = 30x^2$$ V. What is the x-component of the electric field at $$x = 1.5$$ m?
Two long parallel wires 0.08 m apart carry 13 A and 13 A in opposite directions. What is the force per meter between them?

options.why: Parallel currents attract; antiparallel currents repel.
The force per length falls off as 1/d.
Correct. F/L = μ₀I₁I₂/(2πd); antiparallel currents repel.

questions.stem: An LC circuit has a 5 mH inductor and a 23 µF capacitor. What is its angular frequency ω of oscillation?
A 2 Ω resistor is in series with a parallel pair of 11 Ω and 4 Ω, connected to an ideal 18 V battery. What is the current in the 11 Ω resistor?

options.why: Only part of the battery's voltage is across the pair.
Correct. Reduce the parallel pair, add the series resistor, then work back.

questions.stem: A rectangular loop of length 0.5 m lies in the plane of a long straight wire carrying 18 A, parallel to it. Its near and far sides are 0.05 m and 0.08 m from the wire. What is the magnetic flux through the loop?

options.why: The field is not uniform across the loop.

parts.prompt: Using Gauss's law, derive expressions for the electric field magnitude inside (r < R) and outside (r > R) the sphere.

rubric.criterion: Spherical Gaussian surface; enclosed charge inside is Q(r/R)³.

parts.prompt: Calculate the field magnitude at r = 0.04 m and at r = 0.16 m.
Sketch (describe) a graph of E versus r from 0 to 3R.

rubric.criterion: Linear increase from 0 to a maximum at R, then 1/r² decrease.
rubric.example: Peak value kQ/R² = 1400 N/C at r = R.

parts.prompt: Calculate the electric potential at the surface and at the center (V = 0 at infinity).

rubric.criterion: Center potential by integrating the inside field.

parts.prompt: Write the loop equation for the circuit and solve it to find q(t).
Calculate the time constant, the initial current and the final charge on the capacitor.
Sketch (describe) graphs of the capacitor's voltage and the current versus time.

rubric.criterion: Capacitor voltage rises from 0 toward ε, concave down.
Current decays exponentially from I₀ toward 0.
rubric.example: About 37% of I₀ at t = τ.

parts.prompt: Calculate the energy stored in the capacitor after a long time, and compare it with the energy supplied by the battery.

rubric.criterion: The battery supplies Qε, twice as much; half is dissipated in the resistor.

parts.prompt: Describe (draw) how the ammeter and voltmeter should be connected, and how R is determined.

rubric.criterion: Ammeter in series with the wire; voltmeter in parallel across it.
Keep the current small or brief so the wire does not heat up.

parts.prompt: Plot (describe) R versus L and draw a best-fit line. Calculate its slope.
Use the slope to calculate the resistivity of the wire.

rubric.criterion: Uses slope = ρ/A with A = π(d/2)².

parts.prompt: The students then use a wire of the same material with twice the diameter. Predict the new slope of R versus L and explain.

rubric.criterion: The slope becomes one quarter as large because the area quadruples.

questions.title: A sliding rod in a magnetic field

parts.prompt: Describe qualitatively how the rod's speed changes after it is released, and explain using Lenz's law.

rubric.criterion: The rod slows down, approaching zero.
rubric.example: Its speed decreases ever more slowly.

rubric.criterion: The induced current produces a magnetic force opposing the motion (Lenz's law).
rubric.example: The force opposes the change in flux.

parts.prompt: Derive an expression for the magnetic force on the rod in terms of B, L, v and R.

rubric.criterion: Uses ε = BLv and I = ε/R.

parts.prompt: Write and solve a differential equation for v(t).
Calculate the initial current, and explain where the rod's initial kinetic energy ends up.

rubric.criterion: All of the kinetic energy is dissipated as thermal energy in the resistor.
